opportunities.title: Oak Foundation - Letter of Enquiry (rolling), Environment Programme: Regenerative Landscapes / Nature and People
opportunities.program: Environment Programme (sub-programmes: Regenerative landscapes; Nature and people; Marine food systems and livelihoods)
opportunities.deadline_text: No deadline; unsolicited letters of enquiry accepted through the online form. 'Please note we do not have open calls for proposal at this time.'
opportunities.funding_text: Over 350 grants a year; average grant award USD 900,000; 'except in special circumstances, we generally do not provide programme grants under USD 25,000'. 'We generally fund no more than 50 per cent of any project budget or 20 per cent of organisational budgets.'
opportunities.duration: Multi-year ('We generally commit multi-year, core support grants (i.e. unrestricted funding), or flexible project grants'); maximum not specified
opportunities.eligible_applicants: Not-for-profit organisations ('Not-for-profit organisations that have not been invited to apply by a programme officer can submit unsolicited requests for funding through our letter of enquiry process.')
opportunities.eligible_countries: Regenerative landscapes: buffer zones/communal lands in Southern Africa; Nature and people: Southern Africa, Southeast Asia, Europe; Marine food systems: Africa, Asia, Latin America
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: Oak funds not-for-profit organisations; the pages neither include nor exclude international organisations explicitly. Alliance could submit an LOI as lead (not-for-profit international research org) or partner with a Southern African NGO. Terrestrial geography is limited to Southern Africa (regenerative landscapes) and Southern Africa/Southeast Asia/Europe (nature and people); Latin America appears only in the marine sub-programme.
opportunities.lead_applicant_requirements: Not-for-profit; must select the matching programme in the LOI form and state amount requested, total project cost and committed co-funding.
opportunities.geographic_restrictions: Regenerative landscapes: 'We focus on buffer zones outside protected land and areas that include communal lands in Southern Africa.'
opportunities.cofunding_details: Oak generally funds no more than 50% of a project budget or 20% of an organisational budget; the LOI form asks whether co-funding is committed and for potential co-funders.
opportunities.eligible_activities: Regenerative agriculture ('a farming system that's good for people and good for nature') and rewilding in Southern Africa; living-landscapes approaches safeguarding biodiversity and livelihoods; small-scale fisheries / marine food systems.
opportunities.required_documents: Online LOI form only: organisation details, amount requested (USD), total project cost, co-funding, programme and strategy alignment, project location, purpose and short project description.
opportunities.application_procedure: Submit LOI once via the online form. Oak responds within two months only if it needs more information or invites a formal proposal; then formal application and due diligence. 'We only approve a few submissions through our online letter of enquiry process each year' and programme budgets are allocated about a year in advance.
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Regenerative agriculture and living landscapes match multifunctional landscapes / climate-smart ag; EO/AI/crop modelling would be supporting rather than core methods.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Large multi-year grants (average USD 900k) suit staff-funded work, but terrestrial geography is Southern Africa only; no LAC terrestrial window.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Alliance has landscape/agroecology work in Africa; would need Southern African community-based partners and co-funding (Oak max 50%).
opportunities.recommendation: Worth a targeted LOI only if a co-funded Southern Africa regenerative-agriculture/landscape project with community partners exists; very low LOI success rate. Otherwise monitor.
opportunities.potential_partners: Southern African community-based conservation / regenerative agriculture NGOs (existing Oak grantees)
opportunities.next_action: Ask Alliance Africa teams about a co-funded Southern Africa regenerative landscapes concept; read Oak Environment strategy; submit LOI selecting 'Environment - Regenerative Landscapes'.

evidence.deadline_quote: Please note we do not have open calls for proposal at this time.
evidence.eligibility_quote: Not-for-profit organisations that have not been invited to apply by a programme officer can submit unsolicited requests for funding through our letter of enquiry process.
evidence.status_quote: Oak's application process begins with entry through one of two pathways: an invitation from Oak; and the submission of a Letter of Enquiry.
evidence.staff_costs_quote: For project grants, we encourage applicants to request the true costs, including overhead costs, for such grants.

unverified_fields: covers_staff_costs (not explicit; core grants are unrestricted)
opportunities.verification_notes: Loaded oakfnd.org/grant-making/, /programmes/environment/ and /submit-enquiry/ on 2026-11-04. Standing LOI route, not a call; Oak explicitly states it has no open calls.

monitor_sources.name: Calls for projects
monitor_sources.why: Funds mainly through thematic open calls (Sustainable Food; Art) in France and Spain. Only open food call on 2026-11-04 is Tiina (impact loans up to EUR 100k for French start-ups/farms, until 2 March 2028) - not a fit. Watch for research-oriented sustainable food / agroecology calls.

monitor_sources.name: Grant-making process / Letter of enquiry
monitor_sources.why: Invitation or rolling unsolicited LOI; multi-year core or project grants, average USD 900k, generally not under USD 25k, max 50% of project budget. Environment: regenerative landscapes (Southern Africa).

monitor_sources.name: Becoming a partner
monitor_sources.why: Grant inquiry via contact form, then invitation to propose; grants below and above EUR 500k (Investment Committee). Food programme is city/industry-focused and lists agroecology/non-urban food system transformation outside scope - low fit; monitor for strategy change.

monitor_sources.funder: John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur Foundation
monitor_sources.name: Info for grantseekers (Climate Solutions)
monitor_sources.why: 'We generally do not fund unsolicited proposals'; occasional open calls posted on site. Climate Solutions status 'Not Accepting' on 2026-11-04. Long-term strategic grants.

monitor_sources.name: Grant opportunities
monitor_sources.why: No unsolicited proposals; 'There are currently no public grant opportunities' (2026-11-04). Natural Resources and Climate Justice and the Andean Region office fund by invitation; typical size not stated.

monitor_sources.name: Homepage / news
monitor_sources.why: Indigenous-led biocultural grantmaking (Kenya, Mexico, US, Global); mainly by invitation with occasional public open calls announced on website/social media (seen via search; grantmaking page returned 404). Typical size not verified. Low fit for CGIAR lead; Mexico programme possible for partner-led agrobiodiversity.

monitor_sources.name: Open calls for consultants & tenders (procurement portal)

monitor_sources.name: Power of Diversity Funding Facility

monitor_sources.name: Bandi

monitor_sources.name: Contributi / bandi

monitor_sources.name: Our funding portfolio

monitor_sources.name: Funding (calls for proposals)
monitor_sources.why: Funds exclusively through open topic calls, no unsolicited requests; 'There are currently no calls for proposals' (2026-11-04). Has a climate change topic area.

monitor_sources.name: Convocatorias

monitor_sources.name: Grupo Argos Foundation page

Only Brazilian organisations or Brazilian branches of international orgs; projects must benefit Brazil. No edital open on 2026-11-04.

monitor_sources.name: Como se engajar

monitor_sources.name: Our grants

monitor_sources.name: Our grantmaking (incl. Andes-Amazon)

monitor_sources.name: Funding opportunities / RFPs
